title: Differentially Private ATE Estimation When a Known Propensity Vanishes at the Boundary
banked_reason: D0.5.G calibrated tier subfield below field floor; paper-score ceiling 6.5 < 7.4 and not salvageable in scope. Triage stopped before panel soundness pass; dependency, priority, related-work, and stale-prose findings remain.
gap_reasons: The contribution remains confined to one fully known, highly stylized observation design with propensity exactly x^2/2, known covariate and control laws, binary outcomes, and fixed Lipschitz smoothness, so it does not establish a general weak-overlap private theory.

The projected paper score is further constrained by the unresolved priority comparison with central-private inverse-problem and linear-functional results, which leaves the novelty positioning less secure than the mathematical theorem itself.
Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded, or re-anchor the proposal (rewind D-1.2).
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a two-sided finite-sample pure-DP minimax rate for the ordinary bounded Lipschitz class under a known e(x)=x²/2 design, using a boundary-corrected clipped estimator and a legal all-mechanism lower pair. D0.5 calibrated the result at subfield below the fixed field floor and stopped before its revise loop; the panel did not certify soundness. An independent validity check found the rate calculations credible, while an undeclared theorem dependency, incomplete priority and related-work checks, and stale anchored/plain-clipping prose remain in the banked artifact.
tldr: The full-population average treatment effect remains identified when the known propensity \(e(x)=x^2/2\) vanishes at the covariate boundary, but its inverse-weight score is unbounded. Over the ordinary bounded Lipschitz binary-outcome class, the finite-sample minimax mean squared error among all pure replacement-private releases is \(\min\{1,\max\{n^{-4/5},(n\varepsilon)^{-1}\}\}\). A boundary-corrected clipped inverse-propensity average with Laplace noise attains this order, while an anchored triangular subclass and expected-Hamming private testing prove the converse. The risk saturates when \(\varepsilon\lesssim n^{-1}\), and privacy crosses the sampling term at \(\varepsilon\asymp n^{-1/5}\). The exact crossover constant remains an open-ended question.
gap: Weak-support causal theory establishes nonregular inverse-weight behavior, while private causal estimators inspected here rely on fixed positivity or bounded scores. General private testing theory does not compute the observed-law geometry of the weak-overlap causal experiment.
fill: The project pairs an explicit clipped private estimator with a same-class binary causal perturbation, producing matching finite-sample upper and all-mechanism lower bounds and a named privacy--overlap crossover.
